cd /exercise && python - <<'PY'
from forth import evaluate, StackUnderflowError

# Independent calls must not share stack or dictionary.
assert evaluate([]) == []
assert evaluate(["1 2 +"]) == [3]
assert evaluate(["4"]) == [4]

# Truncation toward zero for signed division.
assert evaluate(["-7 3 /"]) == [-2]
assert evaluate(["7 -3 /"]) == [-2]
assert evaluate(["-7 -3 /"]) == [2]

# Definitions capture the word meanings active when they are defined.
assert evaluate([": foo 5 ;", ": bar foo ;", ": foo 6 ;", "bar foo"]) == [5, 6]
assert evaluate([": dup dup dup ;", ": twice dup dup ;", "1 twice"]) == [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]

# Definitions may span input lines; punctuation is legal in word names.
assert evaluate([": a? 7", "; a?"]) == [7]

# Underflow from within a user-defined word uses the custom exception.
try:
    evaluate([": boom swap ;", "1 boom"])
except StackUnderflowError as exc:
    assert exc.args == ("Insufficient number of items in stack",)
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected StackUnderflowError")

# Malformed definitions and unknown words use the documented ValueError messages.
for source, message in [
    ([": 1 2 ;"], "illegal operation"),
    ([": foo 1"], "illegal operation"),
    ([": foo : ;"], "illegal operation"),
    ([": foo nope ;"], "undefined operation"),
    (["nope"], "undefined operation"),
    ([";"], "illegal operation"),
]:
    try:
        evaluate(source)
    except ValueError as exc:
        assert exc.args == (message,), (source, exc.args)
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"expected ValueError for {source!r}")

# Numeric forms and case-insensitive user words.
assert evaluate(["+12 -003"]) == [12, -3]
assert evaluate([": MiXeD 9 ;", "mixed MIXED Mixed"]) == [9, 9, 9, 9]
print("edge cases passed")
